message.content:
**Civil law**—the body of rules governing private rights and duties among individuals—is organized into several interrelated components. While specific terminology varies across jurisdictions, most modern legal systems share roughly the same core elements: | Component | What it Covers | Key Features | |-----------|-----------------|--------------| | **Sources of Law** | • Statutory codes (e.g., contracts, torts, property)
• Judicial decisions (case law / precedent)
• Customary practice & administrative regulations
• International treaties or conventions when applicable | Determines hierarchy; statutes usually topmost, followed by jurisprudence, then custom/administrative acts. | | **Substantive Law** | Rules defining rights, duties, liabilities, and remedies. | *Contracts* – formation, performance, breach.
*Torts* – negligence, intentional wrongs, strict liability.
*Property* – ownership, possession, transfer, easements.
*Family* – marriage, divorce, child custody, alimony.
*Succession* – wills, intestate succession, estate administration.
*Commercial* – company law, securities, bankruptcy. | | **Procedural Law** | How substantive claims are brought before courts and resolved. | Court procedures, pleadings, evidence rules, discovery, trial conduct, appellate review. | | **Remedies & Enforcement** | Mechanisms to enforce rights and compensate damages. | Monetary compensation, injunctions, specific performance, rescission, reformation, punitive damages (where allowed). | | **Jurisdiction & Venue** | Which court has authority over particular disputes. | Personal jurisdiction, subject‑matter jurisdiction, venue selection, choice‑of‑law provisions. | | **Legal Personality & Capacity** | Who can hold rights/duty and act legally. | Natural persons, corporations, partnerships, trusts, NGOs. | | **Doctrine & Principles** | Overarching concepts guiding interpretation and application. | Good faith, reasonableness, equity, proportionality, public policy considerations. | ### Typical Structure in Many Systems 1. **General Part** - Definitions, general doctrines, capacity, representation, agency, and basic contractual principles. 2. **Special Parts** - Specific areas such as: - Property law (ownership, real estate) - Obligations (contracts, quasi-contracts, delicts/torts) - Family law (marriage, divorce, parental responsibilities) - Succession law (inheritance) 3. **Supplemental Provisions** - Administrative measures, consumer protection, environmental regulation, intellectual property, labor relations. --- #### Quick Reference Flowchart ``` [Statute] → [Case Law] → [Custom] → [Administrative Regulation] ↑ ↓ ↓ Substantive Law ← Procedural Law ← Remedies & Enforcement ``` Understanding how each component interacts helps you navigate civil litigation—from drafting a contract to filing a lawsuit and securing relief.
